mechanics.name: Detective's Hunch
mechanics.currentEffect: Whenever a Generator is completed, the Auras of Chests, Generators, and Totems within 32/48/64 metres are revealed to you for 20 seconds. Maps no longer track the revealed objects.
activation: Ends/deactivates when: Aura reveal ends after 20 seconds.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (9.1.0): Set the Aura reveal to 20 seconds and removed map tracking of revealed objects.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: A completed Generator reveals nearby Chests, Generators, and Totems for a short time.
specialInteractions: Maps no longer track objects revealed by this perk.

editorial.summary: Whenever a generator completes, reveal nearby generators, Totems, and chests within up to 64 metres for 20 seconds.
useCases: Locate Totems after generator completions without searching blindly.
Plan the next generator rotation using a broad object snapshot.
counters: Only triggers when a generator is completed.
Object information may be redundant once you know the map.
cons: No direct speed or survival effect.
analysis: Detective's Hunch takes this position because sixty-four metres is a huge information radius, and twenty seconds is long enough to actually route toward the object you care about. One generator completion can reveal the next objective, several Totems, and available chests at once.
The perk is especially useful in Totem-focused builds. Counterforce, Inner Strength, and Overzealous all become easier to use when the player knows where remaining Totems actually are.

The information becomes less valuable as map knowledge improves. Experienced players already know common generator and Totem spawns, and the perk does not reveal the Killer or directly speed any interaction.
That keeps Detective's Hunch in lower B. It is excellent learning and build support, but not enough raw impact for a general meta slot.
editorial.verdict: A wide object-information snapshot that makes Totem and objective builds much smoother. Detective's Hunch is useful, but map knowledge slowly replaces part of its job.
